era_setting.place: Oroville, Butte County, California, USA; also Marysville (Yuba County), Yuba City and Live Oak (Sutter County), the Feather River valley floor, Chico, and Sacramento for the Third District Court of Appeal
era_setting.notes: The film runs from the FERC motion of 17 October 2005 to the appellate decision of 5 October 2023, and its centre of gravity is Sunday 12 February 2017. 2017 IS RECENT, so unlike EP68 pinto and EP69 hyatt the era-bound half of this register is CONTEMPORARY and is the modern-stock shelf's strength rather than its weakness -- a 2016-2024 clip of an American two-lane road at dusk is period-correct here, and that is the one structural advantage this episode has. What is therefore WRONG is not the decade but the CONTINENT and the CLIMATE. OUT OF PLACE, and wrong in any cut: European, Asian, Middle Eastern or Latin American streets and signage; EU or UK number plates; right-hand-drive traffic; foreign-language shopfronts; megacity skylines and expressway interchanges; palm trees, ocean surf, beaches, coastal cliffs and anything that reads as Los Angeles, San Diego, Monterey or the California coast, because Butte County is inland agricultural valley and low foothill. OUT OF PERIOD in the other direction: pre-2000 vehicles, CRT televisions in a 2017 living room, rotary telephones, and any pre-digital newsroom. Declared because EP62 greene shipped a 2011 Range Rover on an EU plate and EP63 shipped modern clips through five green gates, purely because nothing machine-readable said what century or continent the film was in. NOTE FOR THE HUMAN SCREEN: the premise's own precision sample judged 35 of 70 sampled register clips OFF-register, and the named offenders were foreign megacity traffic, satellite tornado imagery, money-rain effects, ocean storms and 3D city renders. That is a 50% precision rate. No machine gate measures it. footage_review_required is true and a labelled contact sheet must be opened by a person before any clip enters a cut.

forbidden_claims: calling oroville dam cases, no. c090941 precedent, settled law, binding, 'the courts have ruled', or a decision that governs anybody but these four plaintiffs -- it is expressly NOT TO BE PUBLISHED and california rules of court rule 8.1115(a) prohibits courts and parties from citing or relying on it (HC-1)

saying the county, the state or anybody else gave people two hours to leave -- the 4:34 p.m. butte county broadcast anticipated failure of the auxiliary spillway 'within the next 60 minutes'. the 'two hours' figure carried in earlier planning notes is unsupported by this record and is retired everywhere (HC-7)

saying that the state gave them sixty minutes to leave, or that anybody was given sixty minutes -- the sixty minutes is the interval within which officials anticipated the auxiliary spillway would FAIL, which is not a deadline issued to a person. the film says what the broadcast said and lets the viewer do the arithmetic

attributing the 4:10 p.m., 4:34 p.m., 4:59 p.m. or 6:03 p.m. broadcasts to the state of california or to the department of water resources -- they were issued by butte county, yuba county and sutter county. dwr is the defendant, not the issuer, and conflating the two destroys the film's own argument

saying the class action failed because the mandatory evacuation order turned out not to be really mandatory -- that is the news-reporting version and it is retired. the evidence and briefing showed there was NO DEFINED MANDATORY EVACUATION ZONE AT ALL and no defined group to which a mandatory evacuation order was issued (c090941 p. 9)

saying that a dam failed, that oroville flooded, that a town was inundated, or repeating the dvids caption phrase 'in the aftermath of a dam failure near oroville, california' -- no dam failure occurred, no flood reached a town, nobody died and nobody was hurt. this is the single fact the entire film rests on

saying 188,000 people evacuated, or that 188,000 people were counted, measured or enumerated -- the pleaded class was approximately 188,000 residents who were ORDERED TO EVACUATE, and dwr's own expert testified there is no known method to enumerate who evacuated and who did not in response to a broadcast order. the film says 'ordered to leave', never 'evacuated', when it uses the number

naming any individual california department of water resources employee, in the script, in on-screen text, in research notes that feed the script, in the description or anywhere else -- the jccp 4974 pleadings name employees in connection with allegations of racist conduct and theft that no court has ever found true, and the motion to strike was denied only on the technicality that an identical unchallenged complaint carried the same words (HC-3)

naming or depicting the former dwr employee whose harassment suit and settlement appear as exhibits to the harriman declaration -- a private individual, a victim, and irrelevant to the evacuation (HC-3)

presenting francis bechtel, jacob klein, chantel ramirez, denise johnson, marie giordano or carol a. gissell as failed litigants, as opportunistic, as having overreached, or with any line that invites the viewer to think they should not have sued. they asked for the out-of-pocket cost of two days and were told the order that emptied their town was too vague to prove they had been told to leave (HC-2)
using the quote attributed to 'shelly clarke, 52' -- it surfaced only in a search-engine summary, was found on no retrieved page, and is not verified
asserting the bechtel case number -- the filing stamp ocr reads as '170v 0 22 98', most plausibly 17cv02298, and the scan is not legible enough to state it
saying anything about what the evacuation cost denise johnson -- the figure appears nowhere in anything retrieved, and inventing or estimating it is the single easiest fabrication this topic offers

narrating anything from the 90-page trial-court class-certification ruling that is not quoted inside c090941, and narrating the twenty-seven-day hearing, any testimony, or any judge's manner -- the trial ruling itself was not retrieved
narrating jacob klein's or chantel ramirez's account of 12 february 2017 -- c090941 summarises only bechtel's and johnson's declarations, and the other two were not retrieved
narrating the contents of the independent forensic team report of 5 january 2018 -- it was not read, its existence and date rest on a primary filing, and no claim may rest on what it says

narrating the ferc project no. 2100-052 docket, or quoting the 17 october 2005 motion -- the docket was not opened. what is established is that friends of the river, the sierra club and the south yuba river citizens league filed a motion on that date and what ron stork said about it to cnn, attributed to him by name

saying in the film's own voice that california officials ignored warnings, or that the 2005 motion caused or predicted the 2017 event -- that is cnn's characterisation and ron stork's argument, and both must be attributed out loud to the people who made them

presenting the 5 october 2023 decision in oroville dam cases, no. c093600 as a reversal, as an appeal by the evacuees, or as part of their case -- it is a different case with a different plaintiff, brought by the butte county district attorney on behalf of the people, and its text never mentions the evacuation and names no individual

saying that any statute, rule, code or emergency-management practice changed BECAUSE of this event -- nothing retrieved establishes a causal change, and 'and that is why today...' is the most tempting unsourced ending this episode offers

saying that a thirty-foot wall of water was coming, in the film's own voice -- that is what genoa widener told nbc news residents were told, and it may only appear attributed to her and marked as what people were told, never as what was true

quoting or paraphrasing any handwritten government claim form from the 'oroville spillway claims' document, or naming any claimant in it -- the ocr is too degraded to read names reliably and one legible claim belongs to a woman whose name cannot be read
saying that anyone recovered anything, settled, or was compensated -- no settlement, verdict or judgment for an individual evacuee was found, and the claims that could be read were rejected

stating whether francis bechtel, denise johnson, jacob klein, chantel ramirez, nicoli nicholas, jeanette morton or connie parks is living, traceable, willing to speak, or what any of them thinks today -- none of it was investigated and none of it is known

presenting any generated image as an authentic record of february 2017: a photograph of the appellate opinion, a page of a complaint, a government claim form, a county emergency broadcast, a phone alert, a television chyron, a newspaper front page or a court exhibit. their words may be SET AS TYPOGRAPHY on the film's own document ground, because the words are public record, but never styled to look like a photograph of the original paper. card, not scan (HC-6, invariant 11)

depicting the likeness of denise johnson, francis bechtel, nicoli nicholas, jeanette morton, connie parks, genoa widener, kaysi or greg levias, bob mulholland, ron stork, marie giordano, carol a. gissell, any judge, any lawyer, any dwr employee or any named or unnamed evacuee (HC-6)

calling the silver dollar fairgrounds shelter sequence or the supermarket sequence archive, footage, or a record of the day -- there is no government-published photograph or video of the silver dollar fairgrounds shelter and no clearable footage of the supermarket from any source at any price checked. both are labelled reconstructions on screen and disclosed at publish
approved_deviations: BUILD BELOW THE LINE. The premise scores 85 of 100 against config/pd_planning_os.v002.json, whose PRODUCTION threshold is 90; the recorded verdict is RESERVE. The owner decided on 2026-08-12, with the number in front of them, to build it at 30 minutes as EP71. This is an owner decision, NOT a weakened gate, and no threshold in the planning OS was or may be adjusted to agree with it.

PRODUCIBILITY: OVERALL AMBER, ERA-BOUND HALF RED. OWNER DECISION REQUIRED BEFORE GREENLIGHT. Re-measured independently 2026-08-12 after the premise was written, against the same shelf and the same method chain. Whole labelled register 0.124 GREEN on a reconstructed 2,092-clip union, 0.201 AMBER on the premise's own 1,293; eyeball-corrected at an independently drawn precision of 0.500 (n=80, seed 2017 -- which lands on the premise's own 0.50 from a separate draw), 0.249 AMBER. But the ERA-BOUND half -- the registers that must read as 2017 small-town inland Northern California -- is 0.512 RED corrected, and 1.600 RED against the 65 clips that carry a verifiable US place marker. config/pd_planning_os.v002.json says RED must not be greenlit without either an archive acquisition plan or an accepted AI-motion budget. THIS EPISODE TAKES THE ARCHIVE-ACQUISITION ROUTE AND BUDGETS ZERO AI MOTION: the rights pre-screen's 4 clearable clips and 26 verified stills, plus 118 commissioned stills. The staging plan is FILM_BIBLE v001 section 10 and SCENE_PLAN v001 section 4.

THE SHELF IS NOT AN AMERICAN SHELF, WHICH IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT AND IS NOT THE ONE THE PREMISE NAMED. Measured 2026-08-12 by word-boundary geo markers over title + matched_keywords + filename: inside the era-bound half, foreign place markers outnumber US markers 2.9 to 1 (190 against 65 of 809); across the whole 20,840-clip video corpus, 6.7 to 1 (2,124 against 315). 554 of 809 era-bound rows carry no country marker at all -- which is not evidence of being American, it is evidence that the ledger cannot tell you. And the 65 US-marked rows are mostly the wrong America: New York, Chicago, Las Vegas, Los Angeles freeways and the Pacific Coast Highway. FOUR rows read as a rural Californian town. This is why 92 of the forbidden_subjects are place and climate words rather than era words.

TWO BEATS HAVE NO ARCHIVE AND ARE COMMISSIONED. The premise recorded emergency_shelter as ONE clip on the entire shelf. The re-measurement found the true figure is ZERO: that one clip is a German WWII bunker door, and a 28-term net over the whole shelf in ALL media kinds returns exactly one video (a graduation ceremony in a gymnasium) and eight stills (folding chairs, a hostel bunk, an empty cot), none of them an emergency shelter. red cross / cots / fairgrounds / evacuation center / evacuee / community hall / church hall / sleeping bag / aid station / disaster relief all return ZERO. The Silver Dollar Fairgrounds sequence is therefore fully commissioned -- 10 labelled reconstruction stills, raised from 6 after this measurement -- and the supermarket opening beat is a mixed solve: about 12 of 38 shelf rows are genuine store interiors and only 4 of the 38 are already burned in a prior episode, so 6-8 unburned interiors can carry it once a human confirms one of them reads as an American store.

CROSS-EPISODE REUSE IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THE POLICE REGISTER. scripts/check_cross_episode_reuse.py against episodes/_planning/measurements/STAGED_CLIP_INDEX.json (6,165 staged clips, 4,813 distinct sources, 55 episode slugs) found 115 of 376 candidate clips already used in a previous episode. police_sheriff_siren is the worst: 97 of 156 already burned, 62%, so its effective size is 59 and four of those are a cowboy sheriff, police dogs and robots. One clip is already in five films. The sheriff's-car beat must be checked against that index before it is staged, not after.

THE PREMISE'S REGISTER BREAKDOWN IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE AS STATED, AND ONE FIGURE IN IT IS WRONG. The twelve term lists were never saved to the repository -- the register names appear only inside the premise file itself. Reconstructed narrow and broad nets reproduce 4 of 12 counts within 10% (evacuation_traffic, california_place, dam_spillway_reservoir, emergency_shelter) and cannot reach the others. police_sheriff_siren = 75 is arithmetically impossible: a bare word-boundary match on 'police' alone returns 143 rows, so no superset containing that word can return 75. television_screen = 38 and flood_river_erosion = 22 are reachable only by excluding the head words 'screen' (307 alone) and 'river' (328 alone), and excluding 'river' is wrong for a film about the Feather River. The premise's utilisation conclusion survives; its per-register table should be read as indicative, not as measured.

spec v2 row 9: the hook is voiced from frame 0 and runs about 22 seconds, not the older 8-second silent montage. EP71 is after EP66, so row 9 binds and this is the compliant shape, recorded here so no tool reads the old 8-second budget.

notes: EVERY BAND HERE IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN. Pace basis is docs/PD_CANON.md rule 25: the measured end-to-end narration band is 159.5-169.7 wpm, and 176 wpm is optimistic. The narration tool's own 'measured wpm' counts speech only, excludes inter-chunk silence, runs about 7% fast, and is NOT used. NON-NARRATION TIME, fixed at 18.0 s: ENDCARD_SEC 9.0 (Bookends, unchanged) plus 9.0 s of DESIGNED SILENCE -- 3.0 s on the 4:34 p.m. broadcast card in the HOOK, 3.0 s at the TURN when the court's finding lands, and 3.0 s on the disposition line in ACT_5. WORD BAND: writing band 4,550-5,000, design centre 4,750. RUNTIME BAND, derived at both edges so it holds across the whole measured pace range: R_lo = 60*4550/169.7 + 18.0 = 1608.7 + 18.0 = 1626.7 s (fewest words at the fastest measured pace); R_hi = 60*5000/159.5 + 18.0 = 1880.9 + 18.0 = 1898.9 s (most words at the slowest). Declared [1625, 1900] contains both edges and both edges fall inside the mid profile 1620-1980 s, which the 30-minute EP69 band did not. DESIGN POINT: 4,750 words spans 1679.4 s (169.7 wpm) to 1786.8 s (159.5 wpm); with 18.0 s of non-narration the finished film lands 1697.4-1804.8 s, i.e. 28:17 to 30:05, inside the declared band at both edges. CUT BUDGET, checked so the contract is satisfiable (EP66 declared one that was not): at target_cut_sec 3.8 the film holds 1625/3.8 = 427 cuts at the short edge and 1900/3.8 = 500 at the long edge; stills may occupy at most 32% of cuts, so still cuts are <= 136 at the short edge and video cuts are >= 291 there. mandatory_stills 114 fits under 136 and distinct_video_assets 260 fits under 291, AT BOTH EDGES. PLATE COUNT IS DERIVED FROM THE SECTION WORD BUDGET, one commissioned plate per 45 narration words per section, rounded up, with a floor of 6 for the HOOK and 2 for the OP because those two sections cut far faster than the film's average: HOOK 60w->6, OP 40w->2, ACT_1 900w->20, ACT_2 800w->18, ACT_3 850w->19, ACT_4 950w->22, ACT_5 950w->22, ENDING 200w->5. Total 114, PLUS FOUR added to the ACT_3 shelter block after the 2026-08-12 re-measurement found the shelter register is empty rather than thin -- O115 to O118, which sit at the end of the id range but belong to the ACT_3 sequence and are listed there in the scene plan and the image order. Total 118, which is still under the 136 ceiling at the short edge. distinct_video_assets 260 is the premise's own measured clips_needed_30min and is NOT a guess. FOOTAGE SUPPLY measured 2026-08-12 over the shelf ledgers via scripts/shelf.py shelf_rows(), video items only, word-boundary matching against title + matched_keywords + filename, same-title re-ingests collapsed, quarantined and talking-head and sub-720p removed: 1,293 distinct clips across twelve sub-registers, of which a 70-clip random sample (seed 2017) judged 50% off-register. A hit count is not a supply count. footage_review_required is true and a labelled contact sheet of the supermarket, shelter, spillway and cattle sub-registers must be opened by a person before any clip enters a cut. THE ERA SPLIT is unusual for this channel and is stated in era_setting.notes: 2017 is contemporary, so the era-bound half of this register is the modern shelf's strength, and the failure mode is CONTINENT and CLIMATE, not decade.
